extracted.intended_audience: general readers, fans, and researchers of television/stand-up comedy
extracted.subtask_description: Describes the format, production, and episode-level requirements/characteristics of the Comedy Central half-hour stand-up series (formerly The Half Hour) including performer selection, runtime, filming locations, seasons and episode counts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Episode feature / performer type
rubrics_metrics.description: Every episode features an up-and-coming comedian or sometimes a group performing an original set of stand-up.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Core series format: spotlighting individual emerging comedians (or occasionally a group) delivering a set specifically created for the episode. Appears across seasons as the show's standard episode structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Material requirement: original set
rubrics_metrics.description: Performers perform an original set of stand-up.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The show expects material to be original for the performer's set on the program (i.e., not recycled as part of the episode's defining content). This is part of the series' positioning as providing each comedian their own half-hour showcase.

rubrics_metrics.name: Premise / talent selection focus
rubrics_metrics.description: The Half Hour shines a spotlight on some of the funniest and most unusual voices in stand-up comedy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implied selection criterion: booking tends toward comedians with distinctive, unusual, or notably funny voices/styles rather than established mainstream headliners — emphasis on up-and-coming or unique voices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Runtime / episode length
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard half-hour television slot (approximately 22 minutes of content), informing editing, pacing, and material length for each performer's set.

rubrics_metrics.name: Production / filming locations by era
rubrics_metrics.description: The first four seasons of the show were filmed at the Royale theatre in Boston, Massachusetts. Beginning with the fifth season, the comedians now perform their sets at the Civic Theatre in New Orleans, Louisiana.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Production venue changed across the series run (Royale Theatre 2012–15; Civic Theatre 2016–19), which may affect staging, audience, and production logistics for episodes recorded in different seasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Series branding and commissioning practice
rubrics_metrics.description: It was announced that a sixth season was picked up with 14 new stand-up comedians given their own set. The show was retitled Comedy Central Stand-Up Presents (formerly The Half Hour).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shows commissioning practice for a season (example: season six commissioning 14 new comedians each with their own set) and the series' rebranding; implies season-level planning and selection quotas when commissioned by the network.

rubrics_metrics.name: Series scope: seasons and episode count
rubrics_metrics.description: No. of seasons: 8. No. of episodes: 108.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides the overall series scale and episode availability; useful as an expectation for the number of half-hour showcases produced across the program's run (2012–2019).
